rename.actual_change: TYPE change (u32 ms field -> Duration accessor) + owning-type rename
rename.resolution: NOT W5-timer work, and not a spelling. Reassigned to the QOS stage: the change is a TYPE change (a `u32` millisecond FIELD becomes a `Duration` accessor) on a type the qos stage is already renaming (`rust:QosSettings` -> `QoSProfile`), so this row cannot land before that one and has nothing of its own to land after it. Kept as `rename` because the eventual spelling really is rclrs's; the block is what stops it reading as timer work.
rename.shard_note: the row sits in timer/ because `--check` derives the shard from the DECLARING HEADER, not from the name; it cannot be filed under qos without failing the gate. The owner field, not the filename, is where the work lives.

why: rclrs 0.7.0's `QoSProfile::deadline_duration(Duration)` builder -- the deadline window. THEIRS-ONLY: ours is `nros_rmw::QoSProfile` (`packages/core/nros-rmw/src/traits.rs:608`) -- the TYPE names MATCHED on 2026-08-27, when the `QosSettings`->`QoSProfile` rename landed (phase-379 W5) -- but ours exposes no such BUILDER. CORRECTED 2026-08-26 (phase-379 W5, group B) -- the previous text was wrong three times over. (1) `ours takes milliseconds` implies a method to rename; there is none. Ours is a public FIELD, `QoSProfile::deadline_ms: u32` (traits.rs:621), set by struct literal or by `apply_override_value`. (2) `there is no Duration type in C++ at all` has been false since 2026-08-25: `nros::Duration` ships in `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/duration.hpp` (issue 0789, commit 2b58bbd38) and is inside this report's extracted C++ surface via `rclcpp/rclcpp.hpp:26` -- which is why `cpp:Duration::from_nanoseconds` and `cpp:Duration::to_msg` correlate in this shard. (3) `the C API has none either` is false: `rcl_duration_t` and `rclc_duration_from_nanoseconds` are ledgered right here as `c:duration_value_t` and `c:duration_from_nanoseconds`, and Rust's own duration type is `rust:Duration`. The cross-reference `cpp:Duration::Duration` names a key that exists in no shard. The millisecond unit is therefore a choice about the shared repr(C) QoS record -- `rclc_qos_t` carries `uint32_t deadline_ms` / `lifespan_ms` / `liveliness_lease_ms` (`nros_generated.h:1527-1535`) -- not a consequence of a type nobody had.
